chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the egg that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) cut in it. He said: It was an egg of iron that a man stole from the war booty, so he cut it. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as he cut the one who stole from the booty and had no share in it. Indeed, one in this state is subject to the cutting of the hand. On the condition that the cutting is waived from him if he stole an amount equal to his share or slightly less than what requires cutting. As for what exceeded his share by the amount that requires cutting, cutting is obligatory upon him in all cases, as indicated by that.

key_terms.البَيضَة: Egg (a container or lump, here of iron)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting the hand for stealing from war booty if the thief is a soldier with a share in the booty?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the specific application of the hadd punishment for theft (qat') regarding ghanimah, distinguishing between a soldier's personal share (nasib) and the communal pool. It establishes that the hand is only cut if the stolen amount exceeds the thief's allocated portion by the minimum nisab required for the hadd, reflecting the Shia juristic view that ghanimah is partially private property. This ruling highlights the nuanced legal reasoning of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in reconciling communal war spoils with individual property rights.
